slides.alt: Cover slide. The Margin-Proof Tracker. Headline: eleven companies say AI is paying off, none can prove it. A five-rung evidence ladder is shown, with the top two rungs unfilled.
The evidence ladder, five rungs: 0 narrative, 1 operational, 2 financial claim, 3 P and L attributed, 4 sustained. Rungs 3 and 4 are shown unfilled. Note: nobody we track is above rung 2.

Scoreboard. Eleven companies each plotted on the 0 to 4 ladder: S&P Global 2, Ecolab 2, Equifax 2, Infosys 2, Alphabet 2, IBM 2, ServiceNow 2, Bank of America 2, Klarna 2, Duolingo 2, JPMorgan 1. The Stage 4 column is highlighted and completely empty. S&P Global and Ecolab are marked with a down arrow.
Ten of eleven companies sit at Stage 2. Bar chart: Stage 0 to 1 has one company, Stage 2 has ten, Stage 3 has zero, Stage 4 has zero.

What Stage 2 means: a claim asserted, never reconciled. Three examples. IBM: gen-AI is about half of Consulting signings, but signings are not revenue. ServiceNow: AI crossed one billion dollars in annual contract value, but that is contracted, not booked. Equifax: AI cost target doubled to 150 million dollars, but it sized the saving and put no number on the upside.

This issue's correction. Issue 005 graded S&P Global and Ecolab at Stage 3; both are Stage 2. Stage 3 requires AI isolated in reported results, and the claim traced to a bank's review rather than the companies' own filings. Both rows marked down. They report Tuesday.

Why the top rung is empty. Stage 4 requires an AI-attributed margin gain that holds four straight quarters in reported results. Nothing in the disclosure regime requires a company to produce that. AI costs land in audited lines; AI revenue lands in signings, backlog and contract value, which never touch an audited statement.

Four questions to run on your own AI spend. One: can a rival buy it tomorrow? Two: does it run on something only you have? Three: is it tied to your operations specifically? Four: will it still be scarce in three years? Mostly anyone-can-buy-it means you are funding a cost line; mostly only-us is where advantage forms.
What moves a row next. Tuesday July 28: S&P Global and Ecolab report. Wednesday August 5: Duolingo. Tuesday August 18: Klarna. The ladder publishes every Sunday, free, at aiabovethecut.com.
